The final step on most tariff bills, applied to the R222,00 subtotal:
R8 000 at 5% for three years: simple interest gives R9 200,00, compound gives:
A R450,00 pair of shoes rising with 6% inflation for two years costs:
options: R504,00 — add 6% of the original twice
R505,62 — 450 × 1,06², each rise works on the new price

subtopics.title: VAT, Income Tax and Exchange Rates

questions.question: A till slip total of R368,00 INCLUDES VAT. The price excluding VAT is:
options: 368,00 ÷ 1,15 = R320,00 — division unwinds the 15% charged on the smaller amount

questions.question: On a payslip, net pay is:
options: Gross salary minus deductions — what actually reaches the bank

questions.question: Taxable income R285 000; bracket: R38 916 + 26% of the amount above R226 000; rebate R16 425. Annual tax:
At R19,20 per euro with a 2,5% fee, a €95 jacket costs:

subtopics.title: Summarising Data: Mean, Median and Quartiles

questions.question: For the arranged marks 36, 43, 48, 52, 57, 63, 69, 74, 82, the median is:
options: 57 — the fifth of nine arranged values

questions.question: The mean of the same nine marks, with sum 524:
options: 58,2 — 524 ÷ 9, the balancing point of the data

questions.question: Q1 = 45,5 and Q3 = 71,5 for that data set. The interquartile range is:
options: 26 — Q3 minus Q1, the width of the middle half, immune to extremes

questions.question: For data containing an extreme outlier, the honest average is usually:
options: The mean, because it uses every value
The median — outliers drag the mean but barely move the middle position

subtopics.title: Representing Data and Spotting Misleading Graphs

questions.question: The five-number summary — minimum, Q1, median, Q3, maximum — is drawn as a:
Two classes share a median of 63, but Class A's box plot is much narrower. The full comparison sentence is:
options: Class A is better at everything
Equally strong at the centre, but Class A is more consistent — same median, smaller interquartile range
Class B has a higher median

questions.question: A bar graph's axis starts at 60 instead of 0. The effect is:
options: A rise from 65 to 70 looks like a doubling, because the bars show only their tips

questions.question: A survey about school-bus reliability conducted only among learners dropped off by car is flawed because:
options: The sample is biased — it cannot speak for the bus riders the question is about

questions.question: A vetkoek costs R4,00 to make and sells at R7,00. The percentage mark-up is:
An invoice reads R180,00 EXCLUDING VAT. The amount that leaves the account is:
options: R180,00 — excluding means no VAT applies
R207,00 — VAT of R27,00 still gets added

questions.question: Why is taking 15% OF an inclusive total and subtracting it wrong?
options: Because subtraction is never allowed in finance
Because the 15% was charged on the smaller, exclusive price — only dividing by 1,15 unwinds it

questions.question: R150,00 paid monthly into a stokvel for a year accumulates:
options: R1 800,00 — saved, but not grown; a stokvel returns what members put in

questions.question: R6 000,00 at 5% COMPOUND for two years grows to:
options: R6 615,00 — R6 300,00 after year one, then 6 300 × 1,05

questions.question: The R15,00 gap between compound and simple interest after two years is:
options: Year two's interest earned on year one's interest — and the gap widens every added year

questions.question: With 6% annual inflation, money kept in a tin at home:
options: Loses buying power — the R450,00 shoes cost R505,62 in two years while the tin stands still

questions.question: For the marks 68, 64, 75, 71 and 22: mean and median are:
Removing the blackout-week 22 lifts the mean from 60,0 to 69,5. This shows:
options: One outlier dragged the mean down nine and a half points while the median never flinched
Means should always exclude low marks

questions.question: The full reasoning answer about which average is honest here:
options: Say the mean, with no reason
Name the median, name the 22 as an outlier, and say which way it pulls the mean

questions.question: The thumb test on the phone-shop poster works by:
options: Measuring the bars with a ruler
Covering the axis numbers — if the axis starts at R300 instead of zero, a small rise poses as a boom
